CFML Language Reference: Functions

ListLen

Returns the number of elements in a list. Empty elements are not counted, and an empty string is a list with no elements.

Category

List functions

Syntax

ListLen(list [, delimiters ])

Parameters

list
The list.
delimiters
Optional. The delimiter characters of the list; the default is a comma. Every character counts on its own, so ", " splits at commas and at spaces.

Returns

The number of elements.

Usage

Use ListLen as the upper bound of an index loop over a list, or to check a position before you call ListGetAt. Since empty elements are skipped, "a,,b" has two elements, not three.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<CFSET Sentence = "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog">
<CFOUTPUT>
<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR><TH>Expression</TH><TH>Result</TH></TR>
<TR><TD>ListLen("a,b,c")</TD><TD>#ListLen("a,b,c")#</TD></TR>
<TR><TD>ListLen("a,,b,")</TD><TD>#ListLen("a,,b,")#</TD></TR>
<TR><TD>ListLen("")</TD><TD>#ListLen("")#</TD></TR>
<TR><TD>ListLen(Sentence, " ")</TD><TD>#ListLen(Sentence, " ")#</TD></TR>
<TR><TD>ListLen("1;2,3 4", ";, ")</TD><TD>#ListLen("1;2,3 4", ";, ")#</TD></TR>
</TABLE>
</CFOUTPUT>

See also

ListGetAt, ArrayLen, Len, ListValueCount
